name: Cordillera

geo.extent: British Columbia, south-western Alberta, Yukon and western Northwest Territories

description: The mountain system of western Canada, divided into three long parallel zones – the Eastern System (Rocky and Mackenzie mountains), the Interior System (plateaus, valleys and the Columbia, Cassiar and other ranges) and the Western System (Coast and St. Elias mountains, islands) – and crossed by east–west belts of lower ground. Volcanic landforms occur in the Interior and Western systems, including shield volcanoes and Ice Age flat-topped volcanoes on the Stikine Plateau.

highest_point.name: Mount Logan (St. Elias Mountains, YT) – highest point in Canada

ecozones_named_in_source: Pacific Maritime (mountains, minor coastal plains; coastal evergreen forest; mild, temperate, very wet to cold alpine)
Montane Cordillera (mountains, interior plains; evergreen forest, alpine tundra, interior grassland; moderately cold, moist to arid)
attributes.settlement_note: Settlement and transport follow valleys and trenches (Fraser, Thompson, Okanagan, Columbia/Kootenay, Bow); passes concentrate road and rail.

limitations: Physiographic description summarised from the Atlas of Canada; the map dates from 1967 (Bostock) and boundaries are generalised at 1:5 million. Lat/lon not given because the record describes an extensive region, not a point. System membership of individual ranges and the settlement note are agent-04 interpretation.
